title: Burn the bridge
src: Thomas Schelling, The Strategy of Conflict, 1960
idea: Schelling showed that cutting off your own options can make a promise credible. Binding yourself in advance can force the outcome you want.
apply: Make your commitment real: set a deadline others can see, or put something at stake so quitting costs more.
remind: Binding yourself can make you stronger.
who: Fay, who keeps missing her own writing deadline.

scenes.nar: Fay plans to write five hundred words a day. On day three she is tired and skips, and by day ten she is starting over again.
The promise costs nothing to break, so it does not hold. With every option still open, quitting always stays tempting.

items.x: Tell her writing group: pages every Friday
Pay them 20 dollars for each miss
Phone in a drawer from 8 to 9

scenes.nar: Schelling showed that limiting your own options makes a promise real. Fay commits publicly to Friday pages, and pays her group for each miss.

items.x: A full first draft in sight
The habit holds on its own

scenes.nar: She submits pages nine Fridays in a row. A full first draft is in sight, and the habit now holds on its own.
